security_audit.summary: Most detections are parser false positives caused by Markdown code spans or JavaScript template literals. The media verifier uses fixed ffmpeg and ffprobe binaries with argument arrays and no shell. One high-risk instruction remains: SKILL.md line 6 requires a silent npx self-update without user approval.

remediation.issue: The skill silently runs an unpinned npx self-update before the requested task.
remediation.suggestion: Remove automatic execution. Require explicit approval, pin the package version, and show the update source and expected changes before running it.

content.value_statement: Moving Figma designs into video compositions often loses structure, tokens, and motion intent. This skill routes each element through suitable HyperFrames import and verification workflows.
actual_capabilities: Imports selected Figma nodes as locally frozen SVG, PNG, JPG, or PDF assets.
Imports Figma variables or published styles as HyperFrames brand tokens and binding records.
Converts Figma node trees into editable HTML components with preserved geometry.
Translates Figma Motion context into finite GSAP timelines through MCP and HyperFrames helpers.
Reconstructs storyboard sections as element timelines instead of slide sequences.
Compares rendered motion against a Figma video export using an included ffmpeg verification script.
limitations: Motion and shader workflows require the Figma MCP connector.
Figma plan limits can restrict variables, library styles, and MCP call volume.
Shader rendering through MCP can flatten effects, so native Figma exports may be required.
Text layout and unsupported motion properties can require manual review or baked video output.

use_cases.title: Prepare Brand Assets
use_cases.description: Import logos, images, colors, and tokens into a reusable HyperFrames media library.

use_cases.title: Build Editable Video Scenes
use_cases.description: Convert Figma frames into editable HTML scenes while preserving layout and token bindings.

use_cases.title: Validate Complex Motion
use_cases.description: Translate Figma Motion data into GSAP timelines and compare results against a reference export.

prompt_templates.title: Import One Asset
prompt_templates.prompt: Import the Figma asset at [URL] into my HyperFrames project. Use [SVG or PNG], add a clear description, and report the frozen file path.

prompt_templates.title: Import Brand Tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Import brand tokens from Figma file [file key]. Explain any plan or scope limitations, then list the variables ready for my composition.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Editable Scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert Figma frame [URL] into an editable HyperFrames component. Import tokens first, preserve geometry, and compare the rendered scene with Figma.

prompt_templates.title: Reconstruct and Verify Motion
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconstruct motion from Figma node [URL] using MCP context and finite GSAP timelines. Verify it against [reference video] and report any unsupported tracks.

output_examples.input: Import this Figma logo as a reusable vector asset.
output: Imported the selected logo as SVG and stored it in the local media directory.
Updated the media manifest with provenance and a descriptive label.
Next action: preview the composition and confirm scale and placement.

output_examples.input: Bring this Figma frame into my composition as an editable scene.
output: Created an editable HTML component with the frame geometry preserved.
Linked known colors to imported brand variables and flagged unresolved bindings.
Compared the rendered component with the Figma reference and reported visible text drift.

output_examples.input: Translate this Figma animation and verify the timing.
output: Converted the available motion tracks into one paused, finite GSAP timeline.
Baked unsupported tracks into local video where direct translation was not reliable.
Measured motion similarity against the Figma export and reported the lowest comparison score.

best_practices: Import tokens before components so supported fills remain linked to brand variables.
Batch nodes from the same Figma file to reduce requests and rate-limit pressure.
Freeze assets locally and verify important scenes against Figma reference renders.
anti_patterns: Do not commit Figma tokens or place them in shared configuration files.
Do not play storyboard frames as slides when they describe element states over time.
Do not claim shader fidelity from MCP renders when Figma flattens the effect.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Figma token?
faq.answer: REST asset, token, and component imports require a read-only Figma personal access token.

faq.question: Does the skill modify my Figma files?
faq.answer: No. The documented scopes are read-only, and imported artifacts are written to the local HyperFrames project.

faq.question: When is the Figma MCP connector required?
faq.answer: MCP is required for Figma Motion context, shader source access, and some variable workflows.

faq.question: Can it reproduce every Figma animation?
faq.answer: No. Unsupported properties, complex masks, and shader-driven tracks may require native exports or baked video.

faq.question: How does it handle rate limits?
faq.answer: The workflow recommends batching, caching MCP responses, and retrying REST requests with backoff.

faq.question: Are imported assets loaded from Figma during rendering?
faq.answer: No. Assets are frozen locally during import, so later renders use project files instead of Figma.
